title: I made an app to go from concept to rigged animation in under 10 min (Update)
author: No-Dragonfruit-675
selftext:
In my previous post I showcased my app which I developed to assist for my personal game development.

Some were asking if it's available to try. Well, it is now, free, and looking for feedback!  


**Why I built this**

Traditional workflows include a lot of time wasted in asset management, bouncing between several apps, iterating on different images and files.

The main idea here is to work with your concepts iteratively while anchoring your design and aesthetic all in one place.

You can go from concept to modeling, rigging, and animation, and even run a quick play test for quick feedback.  


**Regardless if you try this or not, here are foundational tips for asset generation:**

  
For 3D workflows:

**Anchoring is key**: Always start with generating big picture concepts and isolated character sheets. This is how game studios work, they draft concept art and build on the characters and world over time.

**Character sheets**: Generate in A-Pose with a plain background and generate multiple angles. This helps the model accurately generate your idea. Create a reusable base prompt for this for all models.

**Complex models**: One-shot is mostly a myth, you need to split out your model into pieces that you reconstruct. Work iteratively and remember to divide and conquer.



For 2D workflows:

**Create stand-in sprites**: Think dummy UE5 Mannequin but for 2D. Animate your stand-in using a layout guide and then have a model re-draw your character over the stand-in. This is how you can apply one animation to many characters.

**Redraw**: have a coding agent redraw your AI pixels on to a real pixel grid to remove those odd artifact pixels.  


In my app I've built out tooling for both 3D and 2D sprite workflows to accelerate some of these concepts.  


Please let me know what you think, you can try it free at [https://app.tt3d.ai/](https://app.tt3d.ai/)  
  
It's Bring-Your-Own-Key if you care to try.

comments.author: javiergame4
comments.body: Looks amazing, I’ll try it out for sure.  Can you describe the tech doing which pieces?

replies.author: No-Dragonfruit-675
replies.body:
Thanks! Yeah for the main general tools:  
  
**Generate Image**: OpenAI, Leonardo, Gemini - All of their image models  
**Generate Model**: Tripo, Meshy and Trellis are coming soon  
**Generate Video**: Leonardo, Runware - All available video models

**AI Rig Model**: Is a stack of internal tools + Claude or Codex  
**AI Ragdoll Model**: Is a stack of internal tools + Claude or Codex

**Play Test:** Our own WebGPU rendering framework

Then you have a ton of utility and image processing:  
Dither, Redraw, Chroma Key, Resize, Crop, Slice and 10+ sprite specific tools are all in-house processing.

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
I did the same, but my animations are way better and come from FlowHMR by pulling them out of recorded videos, and it runs locally on a 4090.

It starts from a generated image/turn around with Qwen Image 2.1, then goes into pixal 3d -> hi3rd...

Then it procedurally generates a whole human skeleton, muscle/ligaments, all of it and rigs the whole skeleton, realistically, and grows it inside of the pixel 3d mesh and molds/shapes it into place until it replaces it as the "real" one.

Then it poses it for Minimax h3 videos for animations.  It makes a video to do the animation. Then it sends that video to FlowHMR to extract the animation, then gets applied to the model/harness.

FlowHMR is pretty good, you can take any video of anything and turn it into an animation.

Wip, but it's coming along.

Def not the only one working on this.

mines a lot more "1 shotty", generate the concept till you like it, or draw your own, and push a button.

It has an In App AI agent and in App tools, so like you can put google carbon directly inside of the app and it drives it for you. has it's own AI harness on Flow.Ts

Your's is a lot better in the customization department, the arms are really cool! Got me thinking.

replies.author: FragmentedHeap
replies.body:
Flow works pretty well, it needs fine tunes, but I'm sure those will start popping up soon seeing as it's open source.

But I sidelined this for now because running it in a browser is pretty shitty, and I don't like any cross platform UI frameworks.

So I built a whole new engine

\* mtsdf text rendering  
\* origami layout engine  
\* css like styling  
\* html like elements

etc etc etc

I made a really modular UI framework all on top of rust webgpu native and winit, also a sound engine called Resound.

So I'm focused on that right now.

And then instead of a web app on top of a bunch of comfyui containers... I'm going to port all the python to csharp on llama sharp and torch sharp and run it directly using webgpu to enumerate gpus, and directly run workflows right on the hardware without the docker requirement at all.

I'm pretty close to being ready to do this.   Already have the whole engine/framework done.  Working on making html element clones now, sound engine is done.

Everything is modular rust crates with code generated c# libraries, all using .net 11 AOT with the new runtime async features.

Demo App I made with full utf8 unicode 18 fonts loaded in mtsdf and the layout engine runs at about 165 mb ram, so looking good, is fast, runs well.

I'm basically making a light weight browser that doesn't have javascript and uses web assembly for stuff.

I'm not going to support running in the browser at all unless I make it all run in web assembly and support a websocket server.  Probably not.

I'm pretty passionate about abondoning the browser.

But I made it feel like web dev, css with selectors works exactly like css, looks like css, has familiar elements, except all the events, code etc is all in real code in csharp, always server side.

It might change more, still designing it's final form, but making this is my current focus.

And then I'll get back on making game engine tooling.

My current goal is to build a 3D agent harness, where you can do anything inside of the app in 3D while talking to an AI agent inside the app and I'm designing it for Steam Frame/VR and maybe xreal one aura ar glasses, thinking forward to using AI in VR.

If I do 3d modeling tools, I want to make them work with hand controls in VR, not on a 2d screen at all.
